correctness.rationale: Choose a shortest matched interval in the noncrossing source. An interior letter would have its other occurrence inside the interval, contradicting minimality, so there is an adjacent doublet aa. Its loop forces the same doublet in any doubled-label competitor. The possible unique exterior predecessor p and successor q, including their absence at a boundary, are read from the spectrum. Removing aa deletes its loop and exterior edges and adds pq when both neighbors exist; the reduced spectra still match, and the reduced source is noncrossing. Induction on the number of labels gives identical reduced words. A noncrossing doubled word has no repeated directed bigram: an equal-letter loop cannot repeat with two copies, and a repeated distinct-letter bigram would force interlacing. Thus the edge pq determines a unique reinsertion, even when p=q; missing neighbors determine the appropriate boundary, with the one-label word as base case. This proves the decoder and uniqueness also against unrestricted competitors. Dyck matchings with labeled pairs give n!C_n; because all are distinguishable the whole source is optimal. The six words at n=2 are distinct in spectrum, and 311232 and 323112 have identical spectra and equal last letter, so appended fresh doublets preserve a collision. One-letter counts are fixed and fail already for n=2. Independent bounded replay `python /workspace/review_replay.py 5` enumerated full fibers through four labels by position-pair assignments and checked the displayed collision; the induction is the all-order evidence.
